answer: Admit new agents only across a vouching bridge: an established agent co-signs the newcomer and locks part of its own stake behind it for 30 epochs. If the newcomer is later proven a duplicate, the slash ripples back up the chain to every voucher, so nobody lends credibility cheaply. A farm can't vouch for itself from inside its own lagoon of fresh keys, because only aged, staked identities can vouch, and each one has a small capped number of vouches per epoch.
